scope: Official self-descriptions only; candidate research, not admission or product promotion.

candidates.name: Roter Stern Leipzig '99 e.V.
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The club calls itself an antifascist sports project, organised self-determined, hierarchy-free and grassroots-democratically, and rejects racism, sexism, antisemitism and homophobia.

candidates.name: FC St. Pauli fan clubs / Fanclubsprecherrat
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The official fan-club values page says fan clubs oppose discrimination, racism, sexism, homophobia and hooliganism.

candidates.name: F_in Netzwerk Frauen im Fußball
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The official site describes F_in as an international association of women fans, fan-project staff, researchers and journalists, founded in 2004.

candidates.name: Queer Football Fanclubs
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The official about page presents the network as a football fan-club association working against discrimination and for queer visibility.

candidates.name: Alerta Network
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: Its manifesto calls Alerta an antifascist network sparked by football fans and describes antifascist sports fans, ultras and fan groups acting together.

candidates.name: Rebel Ultras
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The network page says Rebel Ultras gathers Antifa ultras across continents and sports and names antifascism, antiracism and resistance to modern football as its values.

candidates.name: Football Supporters Europe
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: FSE describes itself as an independent, non-profit members' association and democratic voice for supporters, with collective action, solidarity and democracy as core principles.

candidates.name: Football v Homophobia
candidates.type: international football campaign and fan network
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: FvH calls itself a year-round international initiative challenging discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity and expression at all levels of football.

candidates.name: Kick It Out
candidates.type: football equality organisation with fan programmes
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: Kick It Out says it was founded to fight racism, expanded to all forms of discrimination, and now runs education and campaigns with fans and communities.

candidates.name: Clapton Community FC
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The club describes itself as fan-owned and states: always anti-fascist, anti-sexist, anti-racist, anti-homophobe and anti-transphobe.

candidates.name: FC United of Manchester
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The official club describes FC United as supporter-owned and community-focused, with democratic ownership and accessible football as core principles.

candidates.name: Bukaneros
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The collective describes its history as defending its team, neighbourhood and way of understanding football as clean of racism and fascism; its official posts also document antifascist and neighbourhood organising.

candidates.name: Progetto Ultrà (UISP)
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: UISP says Progetto Ultrà defends popular supporter culture and limits violence and intolerance through social work carried out with supporters.

candidates.name: Mondiali Antirazzisti
candidates.type: anti-racist football and sport event network
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: UISP describes the event as combining sport, culture, sociality and civic engagement against racism, prejudice and discrimination, with participation across cultures.

candidates.name: Association Nationale des Supporters
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: ANS says it federates French football supporters' associations and represents supporters in dialogue with football bodies and public authorities.

candidates.name: Irrésistibles Français
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: The organisation describes itself as an official association of France-team supporters recognised by the FFF, centred on collective life and solidarity.

candidates.name: GARA – Grupo de Ação Revolucionária Antifascista
candidates.type: antifascist political collective with sport-adjacent relevance
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: GARA describes itself as a revolutionary antifascist collective operating across Portugal against exploitation, discrimination and far-right ideologies.
candidates.politicalClaimLevel: explicit; not a fan group, keep as adjacent candidate

candidates.name: Football Against Racism in Europe (FARE)
candidates.selfDescriptionEvidence: FARE presents itself as a network working against inequality and discrimination in football with partners across Europe and beyond.
